exemplars.title: Compendia: Automated Visual Storytelling Generation From Online Article Collection
exemplars.why: The cluster glyph has an explicit, enumerable mapping: one radial bar encodes fact count and another encodes contributing-article count, making it the only candidate whose evidence directly establishes both named components and their geometric channels.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Compendia outranks MetaGlyph because its quoted evidence reconstructs the glyph’s part-to-property mapping, whereas MetaGlyph only states that mappings and channels appear in a legend.

exemplars.title: MetaGlyph: Automatic Generation of Metaphoric Glyph-based Visualization
exemplars.why: MetaGlyph makes the design of purpose-built glyphs with explicit data mappings and encoding channels the system’s central contribution, and its automatic generation approach strongly demonstrates the pattern’s transferability.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: MetaGlyph outranks FlowForge because the evidence explicitly confirms both data mappings and encoding channels and the entire system contributes glyph generation, while FlowForge’s excerpt names two encoded properties but no geometric channels.

exemplars.title: FlowForge: Guiding the Creation of Multi-Agent Workflows with Design Space Visualization as a Thinking Scaffold
exemplars.why: FlowForge explicitly contributes a novel per-solution glyph designed to jointly encode two named properties—abstraction level and computational cost—making the mark itself a meaningful comparison mechanism.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: FlowForge outranks Conch because it identifies the data properties encoded by the novel glyph, whereas Conch enumerates geometric parts without establishing what any of them encode.

notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting Compendia above MetaGlyph: structural completeness matters more here than MetaGlyph’s greater novelty and generalizability, and Compendia alone supplies an explicit named-property-to-named-part mapping in the quoted evidence. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust any implication that the MetaGlyph or FlowForge glyphs are reconstructable from the supplied excerpts: MetaGlyph’s quote refers to a legend without enumerating its mappings, and FlowForge names the encoded variables without assigning them to geometric channels. Compendia is the strongest evidenced fit, although its paired radial bars may be a relatively conventional composite rather than a radically new glyph form.
